site.title: Prediction Almanac
site.tagline: Every prediction market worth trading, the data you can actually backtest on, and the tools people have really shipped. Rebuilt from scratch daily, so it can't rot.

platforms.name: Polymarket

geo.title: Cannot trade: United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, Germany, France, Netherlands, Italy, Japan, Singapore, Brazil, Belgium, Burundi, Belarus, DR Congo, +28 more

platforms.description: Largest on-chain prediction market; USDC-settled CLOB on Polygon.

platforms.name: Opinion

geo.title: Cannot trade: United States, United Kingdom, France, China, Singapore, Cuba, Hong Kong, Iran, North Korea, South Korea, Poland, Syria, Thailand, Taiwan

platforms.description: CLOB on BNB Chain, YZi Labs backed, covering macro, crypto and sports. Volume ranks near the top but its points programme pays on trade size, so treat the figure as contested.

platforms.name: predict.fun

geo.title: Cannot trade: United States, United Kingdom, Australia, France, Singapore, Belgium, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Poland, Syria, Thailand, Taiwan

platforms.description: Polymarket-style on-chain CLOB prediction market on Blast.

platforms.name: SX Bet

geo.title: Cannot trade: United States, United Kingdom, Australia, Germany, France, Netherlands, Spain, Afghanistan, Austria, Belarus, Cuba, Iraq, Iran, Comoros, North Korea, +8 more

platforms.description: Peer-to-peer betting exchange with a genuine order book on its own Arbitrum Orbit L2; no house or vig, but every currently active market is sports.

platforms.name: Limitless

geo.title: Cannot trade: United States, Belarus, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Russia, Syria

platforms.description: Fast-cycle (hourly/daily/weekly) prediction markets on Base, aimed at traders.

platforms.name: Myriad

geo.title: Cannot trade: United States, France, Singapore, Bahamas, Botswana, Switzerland, Iran, Cambodia, North Korea, Cayman Islands, Libya, Malta, Sudan, Somalia, Syria, +3 more

platforms.description: Prediction market from Dastan (Decrypt, Rug Radio): an off-chain-matched, on-chain-settled order book on BNB Chain, plus AMM markets on Abstract, Celo, and Linea.

platforms.name: Kalshi

geo.title: Cannot trade: United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, France, Italy, China, India, Singapore, United Arab Emirates, Afghanistan, Angola, Belgium, Burkina Faso, Bulgaria, Bolivia, +40 more

platforms.description: CFTC-regulated US event-contract exchange spanning politics, economics, weather, and sports.

platforms.name: Gemini Predictions
platforms.description: CFTC-regulated event contracts from Gemini's own DCM affiliate; yes/no and categorical markets on a central limit order book, settled in USD.

platforms.name: Betfair Exchange
platforms.description: The largest betting exchange; politics and current-affairs markets alongside sports.

platforms.name: IBKR Prediction Markets

geo.title: Can trade: United States, Canada, Singapore, Hong Kong

platforms.description: Interactive Brokers' front-end for binary event contracts, routing to its wholly-owned ForecastEx plus Kalshi and CME; the EEA offering is ForecastEx-only and professional-clients-only.

platforms.name: PredictIt
platforms.description: Long-running US political research market; capped stakes and a small contract universe.

platforms.name: Robinhood Prediction Markets

geo.title: Can trade: United States, Germany, France, Netherlands, Italy, Spain, Austria, Bulgaria, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Greece, Croatia, +15 more

platforms.description: Robinhood Derivatives, a CFTC-registered FCM, sells binary event contracts in-app and routes the orders to the Kalshi, ForecastEx, and Rothera exchanges.

platforms.name: Smarkets

geo.title: Cannot trade: United States, Australia, France, Netherlands, Italy, China, Belgium, Belarus, Switzerland, Czechia, Denmark, Hong Kong, Kazakhstan, Norway, Portugal, +4 more

platforms.description: UK-licensed betting exchange with notably deep political markets.

platform_groups.title: Research & play-money venues
platform_groups.note: You can't make real money on these. What you can get is complete, free history, and that's what you backtest on before risking anything on the venues above.

platforms.name: Manifold
platforms.description: Play-money markets anyone can create; the most open API and data of any platform.

platforms.name: Metaculus
platforms.description: Long-horizon forecasting community with tournaments and track records; aggregates probabilistic forecasts rather than trading.

datasets.name: Kalshi trades (TrevorJS)

coverage.known_gaps: Stops January 2026 and has not been updated since. No order book.

datasets.description: 154M Kalshi trades with market metadata and resolution outcomes over four and a half years - the longest permissively licensed history at any venue.

datasets.name: pmxt archive

coverage.known_gaps: Per-venue start dates differ - Polymarket from February 2026, Kalshi, Limitless and Opinion from May. Polymarket splits into v1 and v2 across the CLOB migration.

datasets.description: Hourly order-book snapshots for Polymarket, Kalshi, Limitless and Opinion, CC BY 4.0 with commercial use explicitly permitted.

datasets.name: Polymarket aligned tape (TimeSeventeen)
datasets.granularity: trades with resolution, fees and event-normalised probability

coverage.known_gaps: Needs the companion v2 repo for coverage past the April 2026 migration. Do not pool binary, up-down and NegRisk markets without checking category.

datasets.description: The most backtest-ready Polymarket tape: relayer noise stripped, resolution and fees joined, binary legs polarity-aligned with an event probability column.

datasets.name: Polymarket L2 depth (vpcapitano)

coverage.known_gaps: Six months only, and no resolution column - join outcomes yourself.

datasets.description: 339M rows of ten-level order-book depth with spreads - the only free multi-month L2 history for Polymarket.

datasets.name: prediction-market-analysis

coverage.known_gaps: A research framework as much as a dataset - it ships indexers for collecting new data, so freshness depends on running them yourself.

datasets.description: Public Polymarket and Kalshi market and trade history with indexers to keep collecting - where most backtests should start.

feeds.name: Betfair Exchange
feeds.granularity: prices and market book; historical as market ticks

coverage.range: live, plus a separate historical archive
coverage.known_gaps: Needs an account and app key. The free Delayed key omits traded volume, and the GBP 499 Live key forbids read-only data collection. History is a separate paid product at historicdata.betfair.com, with politics coverage thinner than sports.

feeds.description: Live prices from the deepest betting-exchange order book, including its politics markets, with a paid tick-level archive alongside.

feeds.name: ElectionBettingOdds
feeds.granularity: per-market odds and cumulative matched USD, by venue

coverage.known_gaps: Scraped from the page, with no API and no time series - figures are cumulative per market rather than per period, and only election markets are covered.

feeds.description: The only free place showing the same election market priced and matched side by side across five venues, including Betfair, Smarkets and PredictIt.

feeds.name: Live Tennis API
feeds.granularity: live match state per point, plus fixtures, H2H and rankings

coverage.known_gaps: Free tier is keyed and capped at 30 req/min and 100/day, and covers live scores, players, fixtures and usage only. Completed-match history needs a paid plan, and the WebSocket feed plus model win probability sit on the top tier.

feeds.description: Live tennis match state and a deep results archive for building fair probabilities on tennis event markets - the event side, not bookmaker odds.

feeds.name: Open-Meteo
feeds.granularity: hourly forecast, ensemble members, historical reanalysis

coverage.known_gaps: Non-commercial use is free without a key; commercial use needs a paid plan. Ensembles are raw members, so you compute the probability yourself.

feeds.description: Free keyless weather API with forecast, ensemble and archive endpoints - the ensemble members are what you turn into a probability for weather contracts.

feeds.name: Pinnacle API
feeds.granularity: pre-match and live odds, lines, limits

coverage.known_gaps: Account credentials required, and no history - Pinnacle is a sharp sportsbook, so this is a pricing benchmark rather than a dataset.

feeds.description: Odds feed from the sportsbook most treated as the sharp reference price, useful for pricing sports event contracts against.

feeds.name: The Odds API

coverage.known_gaps: The free tier is request-capped and keyed; historical odds sit behind a paid plan, and bookmaker coverage varies by region.

feeds.description: Aggregated bookmaker odds across dozens of books including Pinnacle, on a free keyed tier - the accessible route to a sports pricing benchmark.

tool_groups.title: Trading bots, agents & execution
tool_groups.note: Code that trades: market makers, arbitrage bots, agents, and the layers you execute through. Read the licence and the code before you point any of it at real money. None of it is audited and a stale repo is a liability.

tools.name: CCXT
tools.description: The long-established unified trading library, which now lists Polymarket, Kalshi, Limitless and Myriad alongside 100+ crypto exchanges across seven languages.

tools.name: PMXT SDK
tools.description: CCXT-style unified API across 14+ prediction markets, with Python and TypeScript SDKs, a CLI, and MCP integration - one integration instead of fourteen.
tools.covers: polymarket, kalshi, limitless, myriad, metaculus, gemini-predictions

tools.name: poly-maker
tools.description: Maker-only market making on Polymarket CLOB V2: depth-weighted microprice fair value, inventory skew, volatility-widened spreads and a regime state machine.

tools.name: CloddsBot
tools.description: Self-hosted autonomous agent spanning prediction markets, perps and DEXs, with Kelly sizing, VaR and CVaR limits and circuit breakers.

tools.name: kalshi-ai-trading-bot
tools.description: Kalshi strategy toolkit with authenticated client, position tracking, paper mode and example strategies whose losing periods the README documents.

tools.name: Kalshi Trading Bot CLI
tools.description: CLI that researches a question, forms an independent probability, computes edge against the live book and sizes with Kelly - with a demo mode.

tools.name: PolyClaw
tools.description: Polymarket agent skill that browses markets and executes on-chain via split plus CLOB, showing the mint path rather than naive taking.

tools.name: KalshiMarketMaker
tools.description: Avellaneda-Stoikov market making on Kalshi - reservation price, asymmetric quotes and inventory-risk-adjusted sizing, with portfolio caps and Docker deployment.

tools.name: Homerun
tools.description: Write Python strategies, backtest them on L2 book replay with Cox hazard fill modelling, then run the same code in shadow or live mode.

tools.name: Polymarket Alpha Bot
tools.description: Finds covering portfolios across logically related markets by extracting implications, validating them, then pricing the trade on live quotes.

tools.name: polymm
tools.description: Sports market-making and arbitrage bot for Polymarket: de-vigs sportsbook odds, quotes both sides, and hedges the fills.

tools.name: Olas Predict trader
tools.description: Autonomous trading agent shipped as an on-chain Olas service, with separate strategies for Polymarket on Polygon and Omen on Gnosis.

tools.name: prediction-market-agent-tooling
tools.description: Gnosis toolkit for building AI agents that trade on prediction markets.

tool_groups.title: Cross-venue search & arbitrage
tool_groups.note: Finding where an event trades, and where it trades cheaper. Most of the edge in this space lives in that gap.

tools.name: Prediction Market News
tools.description: Cross-venue screener over 10,752 matched Polymarket and Kalshi markets, showing consensus odds, per-venue spread, open interest, depth and resolution rules.

tools.name: Predicts.guru
tools.description: No-login wallet checker, smart-money radar and live trade feed, plus an arbitrage scanner matching Polymarket against Kalshi and Limitless.

tools.name: Chironus Scanner
tools.description: Scanner across all live Polymarket and Kalshi markets with category, volume, price-band and time-to-close filters; free tier serves delayed prices.

tools.name: Adjacent News
tools.description: News and research terminal built around prediction-market data, with a market-data API.

tool_groups.title: Dashboards & market data
tool_groups.note: Watching flow, positions and volume without building your own pipeline. The leaderboards also tell you which wallets are worth copying, or fading.

tools.name: Dune: Kalshi Overview
tools.description: Dedicated Kalshi dashboard covering exchange volume, trade counts and activity trends, without a research-platform subscription.

tools.name: Dune: Prediction Markets
tools.description: Multi-venue on-chain dashboard covering weekly volume, trade counts, open interest and unique users across seven venues - the broadest free venue-share view.

tools.name: OVERROUND
tools.description: Skill-adjusted leaderboard scoring every on-chain fill against the price paid, de-correlating events and shrinking small samples so sharp money is defensible.

tools.name: Polyguana
tools.description: Live rankings across 157k Polymarket markets with 24h movers, a category heatmap, watchlist alerts and a resolved-market archive.

tools.name: Polysights
tools.description: Polymarket analytics suite: market screener, trader and portfolio analytics, a sharp-wallet scanner, and API, MCP and CLI access.

tools.name: Resolve Markets
tools.description: Multi-venue suite with separate Kalshi, Polymarket and predict.fun dashboards, whale watch, contract comparison and a purpose-built negative-risk tool.

tool_groups.title: Data tooling
tool_groups.note: Paid. It's here because reconstructing historical book depth is the one thing nothing free on this page can do.

tools.name: Marketlens
tools.description: Tick-level Polymarket book history from March 2026 across the whole catalog, not just crypto, with a backtester that models queue position, latency and slippage. Free tier, then $39/mo.

tools.name: Probalytics
tools.description: Millisecond-granularity Polymarket history - full orderbook snapshots, fills and metadata via ClickHouse SQL, REST or Parquet export. From $39/mo.

tool_groups.title: Research
tool_groups.note: Mostly papers, and that isn't an accident. Every venue's "learn" page is marketing. The 2026 academic work is free and genuinely useful: order-book microstructure, maker versus taker returns, where prices are systematically wrong, and how much arbitrage capacity really exists.

tools.name: Arbitrage Analysis in Polymarket NBA Markets
tools.description: 75M book snapshots over 173 NBA games: only 7 executable single-market arbs with a median 3.6s life, and combinatorial episodes mostly capped near 15 shares.

tools.name: Decomposing Crowd Wisdom: Domain-Specific Calibration Dynamics
tools.description: 353M trades across 429k Kalshi and Polymarket contracts, mapping where prices are systematically wrong - political markets stay compressed toward 50%.

tools.name: Logarithmic Market Scoring Rules
tools.description: Hanson's LMSR - a scoring rule doubling as a bounded-loss automated market maker, and the pricing engine behind most subsidised event markets.

tools.name: Makers and Takers: The Economics of the Kalshi Prediction Market
tools.description: Transaction-level study of 300k+ Kalshi contracts: a strong favorite-longshot bias after fees, and higher realised returns for makers than for takers.

tools.name: Optimal Market Making in Prediction Markets
tools.description: Derives optimal bid and ask quotes for binary event contracts via an HJB equation, handling inventory and terminal settlement risk - the binary analogue of Avellaneda-Stoikov.

tools.name: Prices, Probabilities, and Parlays: Systematic Bias in Sports Prediction Markets
tools.description: 23M Kalshi moneyline trades: calibration holds mid-contract but breaks in the final ten minutes, and cross-game parlays are overpriced relative to their legs.

tools.name: The Anatomy of a Decentralized Prediction Market
tools.description: Microstructure of 30bn Polymarket book events - longshot spread premium, ~1% wash trading, and a warning that trade direction inferred from the public book is only ~59% accurate.

tool_groups.title: Blogs
tool_groups.note: People worth reading, free and not owned by an exchange. Last post comes from each blog's own feed, so one that goes quiet shows it here instead of sitting around looking current. Building something in this space? Put yourself in this table.

tools.name: Alphanume Research
tools.description: Free quant-flavoured writing on actually trading these venues - order-book mechanics, bonding bots, and how platform rule changes hit short-dated markets.

tools.name: Imperfect Information
tools.description: Rajiv Sethi on prediction-market accuracy, wash trading and market design - the most rigorous writing on when prices beat polls and where they fail.

tools.name: Kacho
tools.description: Data engineer building side projects in public, including the Polymarket market-making bot polymm, and posting the verified metrics behind them.

tools.name: Sentinel Global Risks Watch
tools.description: Free weekly global-risk roundup written with elite forecasters, tracking the geopolitical situations that Kalshi and Polymarket list as contracts.

tools.name: The Event Horizon
tools.description: Dustin Gouker's near-daily free trade publication on volume shifts, contract design, exchange litigation and CFTC/state regulation - the structural risk that moves liquidity.

tool_groups.title: X accounts
tool_groups.note: The only rows here that nothing checks. X killed its free API tier in February 2026, so confirming an account is even still alive now costs money per lookup. These three are in on outside coverage, not follower counts. I checked the podcasts too. None of them qualified.

tools.name: Domer (@Domahhhh)
tools.description: Polymarket's number one all-time trader by volume and profit, around $300M across 5,000+ markets, and the most-cited independent voice in the space.

tools.name: Esoteric Catboy (@catboyautist)
tools.description: Trader who posts positions and reasoning openly, particularly on Kalshi mention markets; quoted in Bloomberg's 2026 prediction-markets feature.

tools.name: Kyle (@KyleDeWriter)
tools.description: Tracks the Polymarket leaderboard and explains platform mechanics, such as what removing the 500ms order delay did to short-dated markets.

excluded.name: Azuro
excluded.reason: Sports-betting liquidity protocol powering third-party sportsbooks, not a prediction market venue in its own right.

excluded.name: Overtime
excluded.reason: Sports betting (Thales protocol family) with an AMM, not event-outcome prediction markets.

excluded.name: Hyperliquid Outcomes (HIP-4)
excluded.reason: Exchange infrastructure rather than a venue in its own right - HIP-4 is an order-book primitive that front-ends build on, and mainnet inventory is a handful of recurring crypto price binaries.

excluded.name: ForecastEx
excluded.reason: A CFTC-licensed exchange that retail cannot access directly; it is the matching venue behind broker front-ends such as IBKR ForecastTrader, which are listed instead.

excluded.name: Iowa Electronic Markets
excluded.reason: Academic research market with $500 account caps, no API, and negligible volume; of historical interest rather than practical use.

excluded.name: Futuur
excluded.reason: Play-money side adds no data or liquidity, and the real-money side is offshore-licensed with 39 countries blocked and no historical API. Nothing in the directory references it.

excluded.name: Hypermind
excluded.reason: Prize-based forecasting with no public API and no exportable data, so it offers nothing to a trader or a builder.

excluded.name: Good Judgment Open
excluded.reason: No API and no data export. Metaculus covers the same ground with full public forecast history.

excluded.name: Rain
excluded.reason: A real venue, but not a measurable one. DefiLlama tracks its retired deployment and reads zero, its own API reports pool collateral rather than traded volume, and roughly half the all-time volume was one address trading with itself.
